statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation and corporate registration via registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, every name used in Quebec must have a French version; the declaration in French is mandatory; a non-French name may be used only with the French version and subject to regulations; the corporate name must include 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' and may have an English equivalent 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'; the distinctive element must avoid false or misleading connotations; official documents must be in French or include a French version.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises du Québec issues a refusal, the filer may file an administrative review before the Tribunal administratif du Québec or a judicial review before the Court of Québec within 30 days of notification; alternatively, a new name reservation may be submitted after adjusting the distinctive element; the registrar's written reasons must be requested and legal counsel retained to file the required motion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a limited partnership only if the general partner maintains a real registered office in Quebec and can access service of process and books; the Registraire des entreprises du Québec requires a disclosed establishment (établissement) in Quebec; a virtual office location may be accepted for general correspondence, but the general partner's registered office and records inspection place must be a physical address; LegalTech SaaS business has no statutory floor licensing, so lower risk, yet tax and commercial substance require physical control and books/residence for the general partner; the limited partnership itself may not use a pure virtual office as its registered establishment without a physical service address; practical acceptance is conditional.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 12%. Revenu Québec / Registraire may verify the establishment's actual existence through targeted audits; risk increases if the registered office is a share/co-working mailbox and there are no employees; for a passive holding limited partnership the risk is lower, but if the general partner is non-resident, the probability of scrutiny rises to approximately 20–30%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2242; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, ss. 1-44; Regulation respecting the tariff of fees for the purposes of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de mise à jour portant constitution d'une société en commandite (Declaration of registration of a limited partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and no escrow account is required. Subscription amounts may be deposited to the partnership's bank account upon formal admission as a limited partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The General Partner of the limited partnership, acting in accordance with the partnership agreement, resolves that the partnership adopts the name; accepts the initial capital contributions subscribed; designates the registered office address and appoints the initial general partner and designated managers; opens bank accounts for deposit of capital; and authorizes the filing of the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and all required tax registrations. The General Partner further resolves to engage counsel for compliance of the legal publicity duties and to adopt the partnership governance rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name search and reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal name search against the Quebec enterprise register and verify reserved or registered names. File a name reservation request via the online portal or in person at the registry office. Attach the partnership’s intended name and statement of activity. Confirm the bilingual name granting and submit to the registrar for authorization.
required_dossiers: A certified copy of the partnership name reservation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new reservation or request a reconsideration in writing addressing the registrar’s objection; modify the proposed name to a distinctive distinguishing designation and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement and Officer Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Self-executed by the general partner and limited partners; notarization optional unless required by contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement setting capital contributions, profit-sharing, management authority, duration, and indemnification provisions. Obtain signed consents to act from each general partner and manager. Keep the original agreement at the registered office for production to the registrar if required.
required_dossiers: Unanimous partnership agreement or separate written consent
Consent to act forms for every general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar questions the agreement, provide an attestation of the agreed capital and management provisions; execute an amending deed and re-file the registration declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – electronic filing system (CLIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the declaration of registration for the limited partnership, including the partnership name, registered office address in Quebec, general partner's identity, and statement that the partnership is formed as a limited partnership. Pay the filing fee using the online secure payment gateway. The registrar will issue a registration certificate and establish the enterprise registration number.
required_dossiers: Copy of the partnership agreement (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected for incompleteness, rectify the indicated omissions, pay any additional fee, and resubmit the corrected declaration electronically. Amend or cancel the original declaration if it contains factual errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for harmonized GST/QST with Revenu Québec and CRA using the enterprise number issued by the registrаtaire. Complete the applicable partnerships information return (TP-600) and request employer accounts if the partnership will have employees. Provide proof of the partnership agreement and registration declaration to tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for refunds or credits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact the Revenu Québec liaison officer, provide additional documentation, or apply to the CRA for a mandatory aide adjustment and expedited registration. Seek a certificate of existence from the registrar if challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Establishment and Post-Incorporation Miscellaneous Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; local municipal inspection if physical office is opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the registered office address (physical location in Quebec) and record the address in the partnership register. Prepare the partnership minute book and register of partners. File any required initial declaration of office occupancy with the local municipality if the registered office serves as a physical workspace. Also verify that the chosen address is not under regulatory prohibition for business use.
required_dossiers: Official lease or ownership deed for the registered office
Proof of municipal occupancy authorization (if applicable)
Consent forms of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal zoning prevents office use, secure a different office address, file a change of registered office declaration, and record the amended address before beginning business activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A – non-industrial LegalTech SaaS activity; no manufacturing or industrial operator permit required
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating license for cloud-based legal contract automation under Quebec's regulatory framework

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – purely administrative and digital service activity with no physical environmental installation, no construction works, and no regulated discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling thresholds for cloud software activity; zero point-source discharge; compliance with general municipal stormwater and light-noise bylaws only.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for cloud data center operations; if the partnership leases an office, the landlord must supply fire safety certificate and building occupancy inspection. The partnership must ensure the workstation complies with CNESST workplace safety requirements (electrical safety, ergonomics, emergency exits).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST and federal income tax administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec income tax administration. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec Clavier d'accès (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-sourced limited partnership doing business in Quebec, obtain an income tax and GST/HST Business Number (BN) from the CRA through registration by filing the appropriate non-resident partnership election and registration package (CRA Form RC158 or RC160 as applicable; online registration through CRA's Business Registration Online portal). Apply for a separate Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) with the Registraire des entreprises and register for QST with Revenu Québec using prescribed forms (e.g., Form SRZ-101, LM-1); provide partnership agreement, designation of attorney, and place of business in Quebec. Once the BN is issued, active registrations for GST/HST and QST are added; foreign entities are required to designate a tax representative in Canada if they do not have a permanent establishment but carry on commercial activity in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. An eligible limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent; income is allocated to partners and taxed at partner level. Specific elections include: (i) partnership year-end election under subsection 249.1(4) of the Income Tax Act to select a non-fiscal non-calendar year end; (ii) filing of Form RC164 (Residency Election) for partnerships receiving U.S.-source income; (iii) subsections 152(4) and 96(3) elections for partnership allocations, including specified partnership income allocation; (iv) elective relief under Part IX.2 SIFT partnership rules for publicly traded foreign-source income; and (v) use of Canadian-controlled private corporation characterization elections for partner corporations, though these operate at the corporate partner level. Hybrid mismatch consequences are limited by Canadian tax treaties, the Income Tax Act foreign tax credit mechanisms, and the OECD hybrid mismatch rules implemented in sections 91.1 and 93.2 as well as various BEPS Action 2 measures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annually in worldwide taxable supplies connected with Canada for GST/HST small supplier exemption; symmetry applies for QST under An Act respecting the Québec sales tax, with a CAD 30,000 Quebec taxable supply threshold. A non-resident partnership must nevertheless register if it carries on a commercial activity in Canada or Quebec and exceeds the threshold; GST/HST and QST registration is mandatory regardless of threshold for non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies of intangible personal property to Canadian recipients who are not registered? No — generally the threshold applies unless the supply is a facility supply, registerable financial institution or telecommunication/transmission supply. Professional legal-tech SaaS supplied remotely may require mandatory registration if the non-resident makes supplies to Quebec consumers through a Canadian retail platform where threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No legislative real-time fiscal clearance, government API stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is in force federally or in Quebec. Registrants must issue and keep electronic copies of invoices in an electronically readable format; large businesses must file GST/HST returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) and Revenu Québec mandates electronic transmission of QST remittances for large registrants. CRA and Revenu Québec provide API web services and secure portals for tax preparers, but there is no immediate government pre-approval of individual invoices. Quebec has adopted mandatory electronic tendering measures for public bodies, but private B2B e-invoicing remains contract-based; foreign registrants may use EDI and standard XML or PDF invoices provided they are encoded for audit traceability.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 1-10 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, zero-rating applies to (i) supplies of goods exported directly out of Canada by the supplier, (ii) supplies of goods exported by a common carrier where possession is delivered abroad, (iii) supplies of services performed wholly outside Canada, (iv) services supplied to a non-resident non-registered person when the supply is not in relation to real or tangible property in Canada (or is in relation to outside-Canada property), and (v) certain intangible property supplies, including SaaS/cloud automation solutions, made to a non-resident non-registered recipient. For QST, Articles 1-3 of Schedule II to the Quebec Sales Tax mirror federal zero-rating, with cross-border export of professional/cloud services exempt when the recipient is outside Canada and the property or service is for use wholly outside Quebec.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency CAD/AD 600 series, through Canadian Export Reporting System for non-licensed exporters) or validated expedited export report
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing onboard/on-carrier dispatch
Commercial Invoice showing value, ISIC service description, and export destination
Foreign-exchange Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-contract evidence proving crediting of export proceeds to the Canadian-partner foreign account
Proof of payment and substantiation of electronic service export (software access logs, digital contract, IP confirmation, domain or user location evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of export zero-rating are subject to CRA and Revenu Québec audit. If zero-rated treatment is found ineligible, the taxpayer is assessed for unpaid GST/HST and QST, with interest under the Excise Tax Act and the QST Act plus penalties of 25% (gross negligence) of the tax amount; knowing participation in false statements can give rise to section 327 Excise Tax Act evasion fines up to $25,000 plus imprisonment and civil monetary penalties up to $5,000 for false representations. Retrospective claim adjustments are permissible in any non-statute-barred taxation period; refund claims and input tax credits claimed on export invoices may be reversed, carry interest and recoverable taxes, and lead to additional business loss for repeat infractions. Evidence must be retained for six years; failure to produce records triggers a CRA requirement and potential deemed-ineligible status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority and issuance agent; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential bank regulator; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/CFT supervisor; Department of Finance Canada for capital-account policy. Canada operates without a dedicated foreign-exchange control licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely; no ministerial approval is required for inward capital contributions, outward dividends, profit remittances, or liquidation proceeds of a Quebec Limited Partnership (société en commandite). The sole fiscal friction is Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced usually to 5–15%) applied by the Canadian Revenue Agency (CRA) to distributions paid to non-resident limited partners. Settlement currency is unrestricted; foreign-currency accounts inside Canada are standard. Practical hurdles are limited to bank-level KYC, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and direct-investment statistical reporting to Statistics Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. SaaS and legal-contract-automation service receipts (ISIC 6201/NAICS 541199) are not subject to customs declarations or exchange-control surrender. Export revenues may be retained indefinitely in USD or other convertible currencies in a Canadian foreign-currency account. For FX conversions above CAD 50,000 per transaction, banks apply standard FINTRAC transaction reporting; supporting documentation (commercial invoices, subscription agreements) is requested ad hoc.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD) + USD Dual-Currency Treasury Suite
Operating Account with Automated USD Sweep

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as a payment-only rail; not viable as the primary corporate treasury account. Canada has no EU-style e-money institution (EMI) licence; foreign digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury) must register with FINTRAC as Money Service Businesses and, within Quebec, obtain a permit from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Money-Services Businesses Act. Since November 2024, payment service providers also come under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) licensing phase-in. Recommended architecture: a Schedule I bank as the sole settlement account and clearing anchor, with an EMI used solely as a parallel disbursement rail after the EMI's FINTRAC registration certificate and RPAA transition status are verified.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC permits electronic identity verification via video conferencing and trusted-digital-ID methods, so no statutory physical appearance is mandated. In practice, Schedule I banks will require at least one video or in-branch interview with the general partner's authorized signatory before opening a Quebec LP account; pure unattended remote opening is rare. Mandatory onboarding pack for a Quebec LP: (i) current certificate from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) showing the NEQ; (ii) executed partnership agreement (contrat de société); (iii) resolution of the general partner authorizing the account and signatories; (iv) KYC identification for every individual owning or controlling 25% or more of the LP or its general partner; (v) FATCA/CRS self-certifications for all partners. If the general partner is a foreign corporation, apostilled corporate documents are accepted but an interview escalation to the branch's relationship/electronic banking manager is typical.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: multiple limited partners, nominee trusts, or silent partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current chain-of-control diagram; full executed partnership agreement; REQ registration extract; register of partners with 25%+ ownership identified via passports; trust deed and trustee identification for any trust-held interests; signed declaration confirming each partner's tax residency and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident control or foreign corporate general partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificates of incorporation; certified board resolutions; notarized passports/driver's licences of authorized signatories; address proof of ultimate beneficial owners; legal-opinion letter from the partners' external counsel confirming control structure and absence of sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection (large upfront partner contribution into a newly formed LP)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partner bank statements covering the 90 days preceding injection; executed capital commitment schedule; accountant's comfort letter (CPA); signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration; audited or reviewed financial statements of contributing corporate partners if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue flows: high-volume, low-value digital SaaS payments creating irregular deposit patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank AML risk self-assessment demonstrating Low_Risk_Standard classification; executed SaaS subscription agreements and e-signature authentication licence contracts; Stripe-to-CAD payment flow diagram; 12-month projected transaction volume and average ticket size; PSP acquirer contract proving reconciliation metadata is appended to each settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner contributions must route via SWIFT MT103/OPC from the ultimate investor's bank directly to the LP's CAD master account at the chosen Schedule I bank. For reports to Statistics Canada, the remittance advice should carry the purpose code for direct investment equity/contribution and reference the entity's legal name and NEQ in the beneficiary line to avoid name-screening delays. Banks require 3-business-day pre-notification for injections above CAD 10 million and may request the executed partnership agreement, capital commitment schedule, and source-of-funds statements before crediting. Stripe payouts for the SaaS platform route via the LP's operating account in CAD, settling in two business days; the Stripe settlement currency must match the CAD operating account to prevent unnecessary FX conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border supplier payments for technology licences and infrastructure use SWIFT MT103 (SWIFT gpi ideally) with a USD or EUR credit to the beneficiary bank; recurring domestic disbursements clear via Payments Canada ACSS (next-day) or LVTS (real-time, for timeliness-critical payments). Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for SaaS disbursements and are excluded from the standard clearing design; vendor payments instead rely on MT103 with explicit beneficiary BIC/IBAN and the LP's treasury applying a 3-month CAD operating buffer to eliminate intraday overdraft interest. Contractor payroll to non-resident individuals clears via MT103 to local payout partners; all outbound FX conversion above CAD 1 million per month should be automatically swept into a daily forward-rate accumulator.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (1-week to 12-month tenors) for converting USD subscription receipts into CAD at budgeted rates, executed under the bank's ISDA Master Agreement and 1998 FX Definitions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for CAD versus illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., CAD/BRL, CAD/COP, CAD/INR) where CAD clearing is restricted; deliverables are used for all major pairs.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term USD liability management (notional typically CAD 5 million minimum, 1–5 year maturity) under an ISDA/CSA with bilateral credit support.
Vanilla CAD/USD FX options (call/put spreads) for known M&A or distribution cash-flow contingencies, limited to premium-paid strategies to avoid leveraged exposure.
Natural-hedging overlay: dual-currency CAD/USD operating accounts with daily sweeps to retain foreign revenues without forced conversion, augmented by monthly balance-sheet rebalancing forwards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Enterprise Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar; NEQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the initial registration; the declaration is due in the calendar month immediately following each anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a late-filing charge of approximately CAD 25; continued failure to respond to a delinquency notice for a full annual cycle may result in administrative strike-off of the limited partnership from the enterprise registry, requiring formal reinstatement with additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is required within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due no later than June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late T5013 attracts a penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, subject to a minimum of CAD 100 and maximum of CAD 5,000; CRA may also issue a demand to file, assess additional 5% penalties plus interest, and pursue a compliance order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is due within six months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed filing triggers interest and late-filing penalties under the Taxation Act (Québec), generally 5% of the amount owed plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; Revenu Québec may issue arbitrary assessments to the general partner for unpaid penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Confirmation Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a filed document; maintained at the LP's registered establishment and produced on request to the Registraire des entreprises, CRA, or Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed annually before the annual declaration is filed; register updates for transfers of partnership interests must be recorded within 30 days after each transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete registers may be treated as a misrepresentation on the annual declaration, exposing the general partner to civil liability and possible monetary sanctions by the Registrar; persistent defects can support a court order compelling rectification or dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit arises solely from Quebec limited partnership status or the ISIC 6201 LegalTech SaaS business. A compulsory audit is triggered only if the LP or a general partner is a reporting issuer, the LP operates as a regulated fund or registered securities firm, or the partnership agreement/lender/investor agreement imposes an audit; otherwise, compilation or review-engagement financial statements are sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP applies: IFRS is required for reporting issuers and certain regulated entities; a private Quebec limited partnership generally uses Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). CRA and Revenu Québec may require reconciliation to the same GAAP basis in computing partner allocations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a standalone annual UBO filing for limited partnerships; the annual declaration confirms the general partners and registered establishment. Transfers of limited partnership interests are confirmed internally and the register of partners must be updated within 30 days of any change. Beneficial ownership of general partners is disclosed to financial institutions in the annual AML/KYC review, and any change in significant ownership that affects the registered general partner is reported in the next annual declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (members' register showing capital contributions and allocated profit shares)
Register of General Partners (showing names, addresses, and changes; equivalent to the director register)
Minute Book or written resolutions register (for partner consents and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110–350 per year for registered office/address services; a full registered-office and corporate-agent package in Quebec typically ranges from USD 250–600 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,500 for a certified audit of a small/medium Quebec LP in LegalTech SaaS; compilation engagements for entities below the audit threshold are generally USD 1,500–3,000.
